title: Unauthenticated screens — one shared shell
lede: The login scene is a fully designed system in globals.css. Sign-in used all of it; the other three unauthenticated screens used only the background and rebuilt a plainer card. Anyone who clicked "Forgot password?" watched the branding change mid-flow.

stats.n: Forgot, reset, and forced change had no heading
Moved out of the card onto the scene

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.note: Captured from the real routes on a local dev server at 1280×900, device scale 2, after entrance animations settled. The baseline came from git stash of only these four files, so the rest of the working tree was identical between runs.

pairs.title: Forgot password
pairs.sub: The screen a locked-out user reaches from the sign-in page.
pairs.beforeCap: A plain opaque card. The logo is 48px and sits inside it, the wordmark is a CardTitle so the page has no h1, and there is no backdrop material — measured backdrop-filter: none.
pairs.afterCap: The same shell sign-in uses: 64px logo and white wordmark on the scene, a real h1, and the translucent card measured at blur(24px) saturate(1.5).

pairs.title: Reset password
pairs.sub: Reached from the emailed link. Same divergence, same fix.
pairs.beforeCap: Identical plain treatment: 48px logo inside an opaque card, no heading element.
pairs.afterCap: Now indistinguishable from sign-in and forgot-password apart from the subtitle line.

pairs.title: Sign in — the reference
pairs.sub: Already correct. Included to show the target the other three now match.
pairs.beforeCap: Unchanged by this work; it already used the full login scene.
pairs.afterCap: Visually identical, but the shell now comes from the shared component rather than being defined inline.

changesNote: Presentational only. No auth logic, form submission, validation, token handling, passkey flow, or redirect behavior was touched.

changes.h: Three screens ignored the design system that already existed
changes.was: globals.css defines a complete login scene: .login-card is a translucent material with a blurred backdrop and a bright top edge, .login-materialize settles it in, .login-rise staggers content, and .login-lockup-title puts the wordmark on the scene. Sign-in used all of it. Forgot password, reset password, and forced password change used only .login-bg and built a plain shadow-2xl card instead.
changes.now: src/components/auth/AuthScreen.tsx owns the scene, the noise layer, the lockup, and the card. All four screens render through it and supply a subtitle plus their form.

changes.h: Three of four had no heading element
changes.was: Forgot, reset, and forced change titled the page with CardTitle, which renders a div. Measured in the browser: main h1 returned nothing on all three.
changes.now: The shell renders a real h1. This is the same defect found in item detail and booking detail earlier today — four of the app's surfaces had no page heading.

changes.h: A 380-character data URI was pasted into four files
changes.was: The film-grain texture over the gradient is an inline SVG feTurbulence data URI. It appeared verbatim in all four screens; changing the grain meant editing four files and hoping none drifted.
changes.now: One named constant in the shell. A grep for feTurbulence across src/ now returns exactly one file.

changes.h: The footer is a slot, not a special case
changes.was: Sign-in carries an "Access is by invitation only" line below the card, on the scene rather than inside it. No other screen has one.
changes.now: AuthScreen takes an optional footer, so sign-in keeps it without the shell hardcoding a sign-in-specific element.

verification: Lint: npx eslint clean on all five files.
Full suite: npx vitest run tests/ — 3628 passing, 0 failing, 535 files.
New contract test: tests/auth-screen-source.test.ts, 5 assertions covering the shared shell, the single noise copy, the login material, the h1, and the CSS the shell depends on.

Captures are from the real routes, not a harness — these screens are unauthenticated, so the dev server renders them directly. Measured per screen: logo size, whether the logo is inside the card, h1 presence and computed size, and the card's computed backdrop-filter.
Baseline method: git stash push scoped to only these four paths, so unrelated working-tree changes were byte-identical across both capture runs. Restore verified before continuing.
notes: Forced password change was not captured. /change-password requires an authenticated session, which is the standing local limitation. It was converted with the same shell and passes the source contract, but has no visual pair here.
Unexercised: no form was submitted. The passkey flow, email discovery, token validation, and error and success states were not driven — only the resting render of each screen.

A first capture attempt returned nulls for forgot-password and was discarded as a dev-server compile artifact rather than reported as a finding. The numbers here are from a re-capture after the route had compiled.

Not converted: src/app/login/loading.tsx deliberately keeps a minimal variant — logo, wordmark, spinner, no card. Routing it through the shell would render an empty card. It already shares the lockup treatment.
Still outside any shell: /support and /privacy are standalone public pages using neither the auth scene nor the app shell. They were out of scope here.
